tools.name: splose_get_account
tools.description: The organisation and the practitioner who owns the API key, plus the key's expiry date. Good first call. GET /me.

tools.name: splose_list_patients
tools.description: Patients (clients) of the practice, filtered, in id order, as short rows: id, name, email, birthdate, phones, tags, alert, archived. Use splose_get_patient for the full record. HEALTH DATA: only look people up when the user asks. GET /patients.

tools.name: splose_get_patient
tools.description: One patient in full: contact details, address, NDIS number and plan info, Medicare/health fund, emergency contact, tags and custom fields. HEALTH DATA. GET /patients/{id}.

tools.name: splose_list_appointments
tools.description: Appointments in id order: start/end (UTC), service, location, practitioner, price, note and the per-patient status (Arrived, Did not arrive, Cancelled, Completed, cancellation reason, invoice id). Filter by time window, patient, practitioner or status. GET /appointments.

tools.name: splose_get_appointment
tools.description: One appointment in full, with each patient's status, case, invoice and cancellation details. GET /appointments/{id}.

tools.name: splose_list_practitioners
tools.description: Practitioners (staff): name, email, profession, role, active flag, online-booking flag, timezone and their location/service connections. GET /practitioners.

tools.name: splose_get_practitioner
tools.description: One practitioner in full, including provider numbers and connections. GET /practitioners/{id}.

tools.name: splose_list_locations
tools.description: Practice locations: title, address, phone, email, timezone, online-booking flag and the ids of the services offered there. GET /locations.

tools.name: splose_get_location
tools.description: One location in full. GET /locations/{id}.

tools.name: splose_list_services
tools.description: The service catalogue: name, type, code, duration (minutes), unit (Hour or Each), price, tax type, group size and tags. GET /services.

tools.name: splose_get_service
tools.description: One service in full, including provider-travel pricing. GET /services/{id}.

tools.name: splose_list_contacts
tools.description: Contacts (GPs, plan managers, referrers, invoice recipients): name, type, email, address, phones and the ids of their patients, invoices and cases. GET /contacts.

tools.name: splose_get_contact
tools.description: One contact in full. GET /contacts/{id}.

tools.name: splose_list_cases
tools.description: Cases (funding referrals and plans): case number, budget, hours or appointment allowance, issue and expiry dates, tracking type, open flag and utilisation alert. HEALTH/FUNDING DATA. GET /cases.

tools.name: splose_get_case
tools.description: One case in full, with its appointment connections. GET /cases/{id}.

tools.name: splose_list_invoices
tools.description: Invoices: number, issue/due dates, patient, contact, location, practitioner, subtotal, tax, total, paid amount, status (Draft, Awaiting Payment, Paid), line items and payment ids. Use status=Awaiting Payment for what is owed. GET /invoices.

tools.name: splose_get_invoice
tools.description: One invoice in full with its line items and payments. GET /invoices/{id}.

tools.name: splose_list_payments
tools.description: Payments received: payment number, amount, date, patient, location, payment method, the invoices each payment settles and credit allocations. GET /payments.

tools.name: splose_get_payment
tools.description: One payment in full. GET /payments/{id}.

tools.name: splose_list_payment_methods
tools.description: Payment methods (cash, card, bank transfer and so on) with their ids, needed to record a payment. GET /payment-methods.

tools.name: splose_list_credit_notes
tools.description: Credit notes: number, invoice, patient, subtotal, tax, total, sent status, items and allocations. GET /credit-notes.

tools.name: splose_list_waitlist
tools.description: Waitlist entries: patient, practitioner, location, wanted services, preferred days and time, tags and active flag. GET /waitlists.

tools.name: splose_list_patient_forms
tools.description: Forms sent to patients: title, status (Incomplete, In progress, Completed), patient, appointment, template and submission time. The form content is included. GET /patient-forms.

tools.name: splose_list_support_activities
tools.description: Non-appointment billable activities (NDIS support activities): patient, practitioner, service, item code, quantity, price, invoice id. GET /support-activities.

tools.name: splose_list_busy_times
tools.description: Blocked-out time in practitioner calendars (leave, admin time): start/end, location, practitioners, type and note. GET /busy-times.

tools.name: splose_list_cancellation_reasons
tools.description: Cancellation reasons with their ids, needed to cancel an appointment. GET /cancellation-reasons.

tools.name: splose_list_custom_fields
tools.description: The custom fields defined for patients: id, name, type (short text, dropdown, date and so on), required flag and options. GET /custom-field/.

tools.name: splose_get_practitioner_availability
tools.description: A practitioner's working-hours availability per date and location (start/end time, weekly or fortnightly repeat). The window is at most 100 days. This is the roster, not the open slots: use splose_find_free_slots for bookable times. GET /availabilities/{practitionerId}.

tools.name: splose_find_free_slots
tools.description: Bookable free slots for one or more practitioners at a location for one patient service, between from and to (the window is at most 7 days). Returns, per practitioner, the start/end of each open slot in UTC. Read-only. GET /free-slots.

tools.name: splose_create_appointment
tools.description: WRITE: books ONE appointment for one patient with one practitioner, service and location, from start to end (UTC). Splose may send the patient its normal booking confirmation or reminders according to the practice's settings, and the appointment can later be invoiced. Check splose_find_free_slots fi

tools.name: splose_update_appointment
tools.description: WRITE: changes the time, service, location, practitioner, case or patient of ONE existing appointment; send only the fields to change. Splose may notify the patient of a change according to the practice's settings. Same input twice gives the same result. PUT /appointments/{id}.

tools.name: splose_cancel_appointment
tools.description: WRITE: cancels ONE appointment with a cancellation reason (ids from splose_list_cancellation_reasons) and an optional note. The reason's billable rate may create a cancellation charge, and the patient may be notified per the practice's settings. For a group appointment pass patient_id to cancel only

tools.name: splose_mark_patient_arrived
tools.description: WRITE: marks the patient of ONE appointment as arrived (check-in). For a group appointment pass patient_id to mark just that patient. Marking twice has the same effect. POST /appointments/{id}/arrival or /appointments/{id}/patients/{patientId}/arrival.

tools.name: splose_create_patient
tools.description: WRITE: adds ONE new patient record (first and last name required). Search with splose_list_patients first to avoid a duplicate. Patient messaging follows the practice's settings and communicationPreference. Not idempotent: calling twice creates two patients. HEALTH DATA: only enter what the user sup

tools.name: splose_create_contact
tools.description: WRITE: adds ONE contact (GP, plan manager, referrer, payer). type, name and email are required (type is Splose's contact type, e.g. Standard; see splose_list_contacts for the values in use). Not idempotent: calling twice creates two contacts. POST /contacts.

tools.name: splose_record_payment
tools.description: WRITE, MONEY: records ONE payment received (cash, card, transfer) against ONE invoice; it moves the invoice towards Paid and is shown in the patient's account. It does NOT charge anyone's card. amount must not exceed what is owed (check splose_get_invoice). Not idempotent: calling twice records two

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "splose_list_services" appears informational but accepts parameters (code) that enable code/file/secret access.

evidence.snippet: id_gt, id_lt, update_gt, update_lt, include_archived, name, type, code, serviceTag

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: splose_list_patients, splose_list_practitioners, splose_list_locations, splose_list_contacts, splose_list_cases, splose_list_invoices, splose_create_appointment, splose_mark_patient_arrived, splose_create_patient, splose_record_payment · Private data: splose_get_account, splose_list_patients, splose_get_patient, splose_list_contacts, splose_get_contact, splose_list_invoices, splose_list_payment_methods, splose_create_patient, splose_create_contact, splose_record_payment · Public sink: splose_list_patients, splose_list_practitioners, splose_list_locations, splose_list_contacts, splose_create_appointment, splose_update_appointment, splose_cancel_appointment, splose_mark_patient_arrived, splose_create_patient, splose_create_contact, splose_record_payment · Destructive: splose_record_payment.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: splose_list_patients, splose_list_practitioners, splose_list_locations, splose_list_contacts, splose_list_cases, splose_list_invoices, splose_create_appointment, splose_mark_patient_arrived, splose_create_patient, splose_record_payment · Private data: splose_get_account, splose_list_patients, splose_get_patient, splose_list_contacts, splose_get_contact, splose_list_invoices, splose_list_payment_methods, splose_create_patient, splose_create_contact, splose_record_payment · Public sink: splose_list_patients, splose_list_practitioners, splose_list_locations, splose_list_contacts, splose_create_appointment, splose_update_appointment, splose_cancel_appointment, splose_mark_patient_arrived, splose_create_patient, splose_create_contact, splose_record_payment · Destructive: splose_record_payment

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
